title: Cut rents by 40% by law
detail: An emergency law cutting rents by 40% on existing contracts, renewals and new contracts. The new rent would be the old one minus 40%, but not below 60% of the local average; homes not let before would start at 60% of the local average.
c: Cutting rent on existing contracts by 40% interferes with agreed contracts and with property rights (art. 33 of the Constitution). Germany's Constitutional Court struck down Berlin's cap in 2021. Even if it passed, in our estimate many owners would leave long-term rental.

s.t: Hahn, Kholodilin, Waltl, Fongoni, Management Science 70 (2024): the Berlin rent freeze

title: Ban buying homes you will not live in
detail: A ban on buying and accumulating homes not used as a permanent residence: for 4 years a purchased home must be the main home of the buyer or a close relative, or a personal second home; it cannot be left empty or let, with narrow exceptions such as social rental or work mobility. On the islands, extra limits for non-residents regardless of nationality.
c: A general ban on buying homes for purposes other than living in them breaches arts. 33 and 38 of the Constitution and EU free movement of capital. In our estimate it would hit many small owners whose second flat is their savings.

title: Ban tourist flats
detail: End tourist use of residential flats (*vivienda turística*) while the housing emergency lasts: gradual withdrawal of existing licences and no new ones. Illegal tourist flats would pass free of charge to a public housing company, with an indefinite moratorium on new hotel beds in mass-tourism areas.
c: As with Sumar: licences belong to regions and town halls, and the state lacks the power. Tourism is one of the largest sectors, so expect conflict with regions and business.

title: Bring seasonal and room lets under rental law
detail: Seasonal lets (*alquiler de temporada*) and room lets would come under the Urban Leases Law (*LAU*) at once, so they cannot be used to get around rent limits.
c: Closing the seasonal-let loophole is a simple change to the LAU, and PSOE supports it too. Realistic.
pos: Closes the loophole used to get around rent caps.
neg: Harder for students and workers on the move to find temporary housing.

title: Make the large fortunes tax permanent
detail: Extend the large fortunes tax to everyone liable for wealth tax (*Impuesto del Patrimonio*), so regions cannot scrap it: the temporary solidarity tax (*ITSGF*) becomes a permanent state tax with the same parameters. Owner-run company shares would lose their exemption above €100 million.
c: The solidarity tax already does this for fortunes above €3 million; making it permanent is realistic by ordinary law. PP-run regions will object.
pos: Regions cannot zero out wealth tax, which reduces tax competition between them.
neg: In our estimate, an incentive for wealth to move abroad; revenue is modest.

s.t: Ley 38/2022: solidarity tax on large fortunes, bank and energy levies (BOE)

title: Abolish the Beckham law
detail: Fully abolish the special regime (*Ley Beckham*) under which people who move to Spain to work pay noticeably less tax than ordinary taxpayers for 6 years.
c: An ordinary law is enough. The downside: Spain loses a tool for attracting specialists, and several EU countries have similar regimes.
pos: Equal treatment of taxpayers and more revenue.
neg: Harder for Spain to attract specialists and executives, in competition with countries offering similar breaks.

title: Lower VAT on everyday services
detail: 10% VAT on hairdressers; 10% (falling to 4%) on vets; 5% instead of 10% on theatre, dance, circus and concert tickets; a reduced rate for artists working through co-operatives (21% today); and no VAT on menstrual products.
c: The EU directive allows reduced rates on these services. The cost is small.
pos: Everyday services such as vets and hairdressers get cheaper.
neg: Lost revenue; VAT cuts are rarely passed on to prices in full.

title: Leave NATO and close the US bases at Rota and Morón
detail: Seek to leave NATO (*OTAN*) by withdrawing from the North Atlantic Treaty, and end the US military presence in Spain, including the Rota naval base and Morón air base.
c: Withdrawal from the treaty is possible (art. 13) with authorisation from parliament (arts. 94 and 96.2 of the Constitution); a referendum is not required and would be consultative (art. 92), as in 1986. Congress will not vote to leave: PSOE, PP and Vox are against. The bases rest on a bilateral treaty with the US.

title: Minimum wage up to €1,800 a month
detail: Raise the minimum wage (*SMI*) to €1,800 a month within one parliament, and by law to no less than 75% of the median wage.
c: The government sets the SMI by decree, so it is technically simple. But going from €1,221 (14 payments, 2026) to €1,800 in four years is almost +50%. Banco de España found that after the 2019 SMI rise, employment of low earners grew more slowly.

s.t: Real Decreto 126/2026: 2026 minimum wage of €1,221 a month (BOE)
Banco de España, Occasional Paper 2113 (2021): effects of the 2019 SMI rise

title: 30-hour working week with no pay cut
detail: Cut the working week to 30 hours within the parliament, starting with 35; a four-day week where the job allows; two days of remote work a week wherever possible.
c: Even 37.5 hours failed in Congress in 2025. As far as we know, no EU country has moved to 30 hours with no pay cut in four years.

s.t: Congress, BOCG 15-A-58-3: 37.5-hour bill returned to the government (10 Sep 2025)

title: Lower the retirement age to 63
detail: Lower the ordinary retirement age (*jubilación*) to 63, keeping pensions sustainable and adequate with money from the state budget.
c: Retirement at 63 while life expectancy rises would, in our estimate, cost 2–3% of GDP a year more. It conflicts with commitments to the EU on pension sustainability.

title: Scrap the cap on social security contributions
detail: Abolish the maximum contribution base (*base máxima de cotización*) and introduce contributions that rise with income and company profits.
c: The maximum base has been rising since 2023; abolishing it while pensions stay capped would turn contributions into a tax. Business is against.
pos: More money for social security and a fairer spread of the burden.
neg: Costly for high earners, an incentive to pay them outside salary; disproportionate while pensions remain capped.

s.t: Real Decreto-ley 2/2023: pension reform, MEI and contribution cap (BOE)

title: Citizenship after 1 year, the vote and a Spanish ID card
detail: Anyone who lives and works in Spain should get a Spanish ID card (*DNI*) and the vote; reform art. 22 of the Civil Code so the residence requirement falls to one year for those who prove *arraigo* (settled ties); scrap fees that hinder regularisation and citizenship.
c: Citizenship after one year would, in our estimate, be shorter than almost anywhere in the EU; votes for foreigners in general elections require constitutional reform (art. 13.2).

title: A permanent regularisation procedure
detail: A permanent route to legal status based on social, family and community ties, not only a job contract; broader proof of residence (*padrón*, travel passes, medical records), as in the 2026 extraordinary regularisation; automatic renewal of permits when the administration is late and the conditions are met.
c: As with Sumar: an organic law, which needs PSOE and the nationalist parties.
pos: Fewer people in the shadow economy: more tax and contributions, less exploitation.
neg: A permanent route may strengthen the "pull effect" (evidence on its size is disputed), and puts heavy pressure on offices, as in the 2026 regularisation (1.17 million applications).

s.t: La Moncloa, 2 Jul 2026: 1,174,978 regularisation applications filed
